name: Fractional CFO
description: Part-time senior finance leadership for SMEs that need CFO-level strategic and commercial capability but cannot justify or afford a full-time hire. Combines financial strategy, management reporting, forecasting, and board-level communication in a structured monthly retainer.
target_customer: Owner-managed and PE-backed SMEs with £1m–£20m revenue, typically post-initial growth phase where financial decisions are becoming more complex and the gap between bookkeeping and strategic finance is visible.
target_buyer: Founder, CEO, or Managing Director
core_service: Monthly management accounts interpretation and narrative
Cashflow forecasting and working capital management
Board and investor reporting and communication
Financial decision support (pricing, investment, cost base)
Banking relationship management and covenant monitoring

pricing_range.notes: Typically 1–2 days/month. Higher end for PE-backed or more complex situations.

sales_motion: Accountant and business advisor introductions (highest conversion). Peer referral from CFO/FD network. LinkedIn content targeting SME founders.
proof_notes: Client must trust this person to represent the business financially to their board, bank, and investors. Credentials, sector experience, and references matter.
failure_modes: Scope creep into operational management accounting, undermining advisory positioning and rate
Being treated as a bookkeeper rather than strategic advisor by unsophisticated buyers
Underpricing due to impostor syndrome about claiming the CFO title
Over-reliance on one large client, creating income dependency
Clients who don't value strategic input and only want compliance reporting
expansion_path: Deeper advisory retainer; FD on record role; M&A financial support; fundraising advisory

name: Cashflow & Working Capital Specialist

target_customer: SMEs experiencing cashflow pressure, seasonal businesses, businesses in growth mode outrunning their cash, businesses preparing for a bank review or refinancing.
target_buyer: Founder, CEO, Finance Director, or Managing Director
core_service: 13-week rolling cashflow model build and maintenance
Working capital diagnostic and optimisation (debtors, creditors, stock)
Cash conversion cycle analysis and improvement
Bank covenant monitoring and compliance support
Short-term cash crisis management and communication support

pricing_range.notes: Initial diagnostic and model build. Monthly retainer of £1,000–£2,000 for ongoing monitoring.

sales_motion: Accountant referrals (highest conversion — accountants see cashflow problems before the business does). Business advisory introductions. Direct LinkedIn content on cashflow management.
proof_notes: The deliverable (a working cashflow model with clear recommendations) speaks for itself quickly. Outcome is visible within weeks.
failure_modes: Being pulled into a situation that is really an insolvency problem — managing expectations is critical
Underpricing urgent work: acute pain justifies premium pricing, not discounting
Clients who fix the immediate problem and disengage before a retainer relationship forms
Getting blamed for cashflow problems that were already baked in before engagement started
expansion_path: Fractional CFO retainer; FP&A build; financial planning engagement; treasury advisory

name: Strategy & Growth Advisor
description: Ongoing strategic advisory for owner-managed and mid-market businesses. Provides the thinking partnership, analytical rigour, and structured challenge that growing business leaders often lack access to internally. Deepest trust of all the business models — and the hardest to sell.
target_customer: Owner-managed businesses with £2m–£30m revenue. Businesses at strategic inflection points: new market entry, post-growth plateau, acquisition or exit preparation. Leaders who want a trusted external thought partner.
target_buyer: Founder, CEO, or MD
core_service: Ongoing strategic dialogue and decision support

failure_modes: Extremely long sales cycle depleting cashflow before first retainer payment
Being unable to demonstrate ROI to financially-focused owners who question the cost
Being replaced when financial pressures increase and discretionary spend is cut
Too broad a positioning making it impossible to build a pipeline efficiently
Conflating strategy advisory with management consulting and underselling the advisory component

name: Corporate Tax Advisory
description: Part-time or project-based corporate tax advisory for SMEs and mid-market businesses, covering R&D relief claims, HMRC correspondence, group structure tax efficiency, and transaction tax support. The independent professional acts as the fractional tax lead or subject matter expert, embedded into the finance function or advising on discrete tax challenges. Buyers are growing businesses that need sophisticated tax optimisation but can't justify permanent senior tax headcount.
target_customer: SMEs and mid-market businesses (£5m–£100m revenue) with complex tax positions, R&D spend, multi-entity structures, or growth through acquisition. Sectors: software, manufacturing, professional services, life sciences.
target_buyer: Finance Director, CFO, or Chief Accountant — occasionally the CEO if finance capacity is very thin.
core_service: R&D relief claim preparation, documentation, and HMRC negotiation
Group structure and transfer pricing optimisation analysis
Transaction tax structuring (M&A, IP migration, group restructures)
Tax position reviews and risk identification
Tax planning and scenario modelling for growth initiatives

pricing_range.notes: Retainers typically £1,000–£2,500/month for ongoing advisory and light compliance; project work (R&D claims, transactions) commands £3,000–£15,000 depending on complexity and deal size. Pricing drivers: business complexity, transaction frequency, HMRC controversy risk, group size.

sales_motion: Warm introductions from accountants, investment banks, and corporate finance advisors who encounter tax as a blocker. Often triggered by a specific event: planned acquisition, R&D project trigger, group restructure, or HMRC challenge. Conversion driver: demonstrated technical credibility and existing relationships with the company's auditor or main bank.
proof_notes: Buyer expects case studies of similar group structures or R&D claims. Professional indemnity insurance mandatory. Prior big-4 or mid-tier firm experience essential. HMRC correspondence wins and settlement outcomes highly persuasive.
failure_modes: Regulatory and technical complexity changes (tax law updates, HMRC policy shifts) make expertise obsolete if not actively maintained.
HMRC relationship damage: a poor claim or aggressive position can burn bridges with the buyer's tax authority contact.
Commoditisation risk: as businesses mature, tax work often flows to Big 4 firms or larger outsourced providers.
Timing misalignment: R&D and transaction tax work is lumpy; retainer income alone may not sustain the model without supplementary services.
Conflict of interest: if acting for multiple competitors in the same market, buyer confidence erodes.
expansion_path: Natural expansion into transaction advisory (financial due diligence), treasury advisory (managing tax implications of FX/cash), or fractional CFO for clients who value the tax insight. Some advisors build a practice around post-acquisition integration and tax harmonisation.

name: VAT & Indirect Tax Advisory
description: Specialist VAT and indirect tax advisory for growing businesses, covering VAT health checks, partial exemption calculations, cross-border supply chain optimisation, and customs/duty advisory. The independent professional helps businesses navigate VAT compliance, reclaim positions, and optimise tax efficiency across import/export and supply chains. Ideal for businesses scaling internationally or operating complex exemption models.
target_customer: SMEs to mid-market businesses (£3m–£75m revenue) with cross-border supply chains, multiple trading entities, or partial exemption complexity. Sectors: e-commerce, imports/exports, professional services with EU clients, manufacturing with intra-group supply.
target_buyer: Finance Director, Head of Finance Operations, or Finance Manager — sometimes the accountant/outsourced controller raising the brief.
core_service: VAT health checks and compliance reviews
Partial exemption calculations and reclaim position reviews
Cross-border supply chain VAT optimisation (intra-EU and third-country)
Customs and duty advisory for imports and supply chain restructure
HMRC VAT dispute and correspondence support
VAT and duty training for finance team

pricing_range.notes: Project-based work (health checks, supply chain reviews) typically ranges £2,000–£8,000. Day-rates (£600–£1,200) used for ongoing support, training, and HMRC liaison. Retainers (£500–£1,500/month) offered to businesses with frequent VAT planning needs. Pricing drivers: supply chain complexity, cross-border volume, disputed or high-risk positions.

sales_motion: Triggered by business events: new export market entry, supply chain restructure, planned merger, or HMRC VAT audit notice. Sold through accountant referrals, trade associations, and supply chain consultants. Conversion mechanism: quick diagnostic call showing immediate VAT reclaim or compliance opportunity (e.g. 'you've overpaid £50k VAT this year').
proof_notes: Buyer wants evidence of successful partial exemption or cross-border restructures. Prior Big 4 or mid-tier VAT experience, or relevant HMRC engagement history. Testimonials from fellow finance directors in similar sectors persuasive. Professional indemnity insurance critical.
failure_modes: Brexit impact volatility: customs and duty rules shift frequently; knowledge can become outdated without active sector tracking.
HMRC position unpredictability: VAT interpretations can shift; a strategy that works today may face challenge next year.
Commoditisation: VAT work increasingly handled by software, accounting firms, and offshore providers.
Client finance maturity: smaller businesses lack the accounting infrastructure to implement complex partial exemption or supply chain optimisations.
Lumpy revenue: VAT work is project-driven; retainer uptake is low, leading to feast-famine cycles.
expansion_path: Expansion into international trade advisory, customs brokerage advisory, or full indirect tax advisory (excise, stamp duty). Many advisors also build capability in transfer pricing, which is adjacent. Some shift into broader supply chain cost optimisation.

description: Fractional treasury function for mid-market businesses, providing expert oversight and execution of cash positioning, FX exposure management, bank facility management, covenant monitoring, and treasury policy design. target_customer: Mid-market businesses (£20m–£300m revenue) with multi-currency operations, bank facilities, or active FX exposure. Sectors: manufacturing, professional services, life sciences, tech scale-ups, distribution/logistics.
target_buyer: CFO, Finance Director, or Group Treasurer — occasionally the CEO in smaller groups with significant cash positions.
core_service: FX exposure identification and hedging strategy design
Covenant monitoring and EBITDA bridge management
Treasury policy design and cash management procedures
Liquidity planning and working capital optimisation

pricing_range.notes: Retainers typically £1,500–£4,000/month depending on cash complexity, FX exposure, facility size, and reporting frequency. Pricing drivers: facility size, FX volatility exposure, covenant tightness, transaction frequency.

sales_motion: Triggered by corporate events: bank refinance, new facility negotiation, M&A close, or management change. Sold through bank relationship managers, corporate finance advisors, and CFO networks. Conversion mechanism: initial treasury review identifying cash inefficiency, covenant risk, or FX exposure; quick wins build credibility and justify retainer.
proof_notes: Buyer expects deep treasury experience (Big 4, bank treasury team, or prior in-house treasurer role). References from other CFOs/treasurers essential. Evidence of successful facility negotiations and hedging implementation persuasive. Professional indemnity insurance mandatory.
failure_modes: Market volatility exposure: major FX or interest rate moves can expose poor hedging decisions; liability risk if buyer blames advisor.
Bank relationship politics: if advisor recommends facility change or new bank, existing banking relationship can fracture.
Cash flow unpredictability: in downturns, tight covenants and cash crunches can trigger disputes over advisor recommendations.
Regulatory change: new accounting standards (IFRS 9, IFRS 16) and ESG reporting requirements shift treasury practice; knowledge gaps emerge.
Commoditisation risk: large finance teams and banks increasingly provide treasury advisory in-house; retainer value justification erodes.
expansion_path: Natural expansion into fractional CFO, credit risk advisory, or transaction advisory (funding restructures, refinance). Some advisors expand into ESG/carbon accounting and sustainability reporting.

name: Transaction Advisory
description: Buy-side or sell-side advisory for M&A transactions, providing financial due diligence leadership, deal structuring input, management information review, and SPA negotiation support. The independent professional acts as the deal finance lead or due diligence sponsor, embedded into the transaction team alongside investment advisors and legal counsel. Broader than financial due diligence alone, encompassing working capital analysis, synergy quantification, and financing planning.
target_customer: Mid-market businesses (£20m–£500m enterprise value) undergoing M&A or PE-backed owners executing add-on acquisitions. Buyers: growth-stage businesses, private equity portfolios, strategic acquirers.
target_buyer: CFO, M&A Director, or investment sponsor (PE partner) — occasionally the Chief Financial Officer on acquisition team.
core_service: Financial due diligence leadership and reporting
Working capital and cash conversion analysis
Management information and financial control review
SPA commercial negotiation and payment mechanics support

pricing_range.notes: Per-deal fees typically £5,000–£30,000 depending on target size, complexity, and scope. Smaller buy-side support (£20m target) £5,000–£10,000; full due diligence leadership on complex target (£100m+) £20,000–£30,000. Some advisors work on time-and-materials basis (£800–£1,500/day); success-fee augmentation (% of deal value) occasionally offered. Pricing drivers: deal size, target complexity, exclusivity period duration, number of workstreams.

sales_motion: Triggered by transaction announcement or confidential process launch. Sold by investment banks, corporate finance boutiques, and PE firms as part of deal advisory team. Conversion mechanism: track record of clean due diligence reports, speed of turnaround, and ability to credibly challenge management assumptions.
proof_notes: Buyer expects evidence of prior M&A experience (Big 4 transaction team, investment bank, or in-house corporate finance). References from PE firms, investment banks, or prior transaction counterparties essential. Deal examples (anonymised) and quality of due diligence reports persuasive. Professional indemnity insurance mandatory; D&O liability coverage recommended.
failure_modes: Deal termination or renegotiation: if advisor's due diligence findings trigger buyer pushback or price re-negotiation, advisor may be scapegoated.
Information asymmetry mismanagement: miss of material financial issue (hidden liability, customer concentration) damages credibility and creates liability exposure.
Scope creep and timeline pressure: transactions move at pace; inadequate resource planning leads to missed findings or burnout.
Conflict of interest: if advisor has conflicting interests (vendor relationships, prior dealings with target), independence questioned and engagement at risk.
Commoditisation: larger firms and Big 4 increasingly commoditise M&A support; fee compression on smaller deals.
expansion_path: Expansion into post-deal integration advisory, earn-out management, or broader corporate finance advisory. Many advisors expand into sell-side advisory (preparing a business for sale, vendor due diligence).

name: Actuarial Consulting
description: Independent actuarial advice spanning insurance pricing and reserving reviews, pension scheme actuarial work, Solvency II advisory, and risk quantification for non-insurance contexts. The independent actuary acts as the specialist advisor or part-time function, supporting businesses with complex longevity, mortality, or catastrophic risk exposures. Ideal for insurers, pension schemes, large employers, and infrastructure projects with contingency quantification needs.
target_customer: Insurance firms, pension schemes, large employers (1,000+ staff), and infrastructure project consortiums requiring actuarial expertise. Sectors: insurance, pension administration, life sciences, utilities, construction.
target_buyer: Chief Risk Officer, Finance Director, Pension Scheme Trustee Chair, or Head of Reserving — sometimes the Actuarial Function Holder or Scheme Actuary.
core_service: Insurance pricing and loss ratio analysis
Claims reserving reviews and IBNR modelling
Pension scheme valuation and advice (DB, DC, hybrid)
Solvency II capital requirement calculations and advisory

pricing_range.notes: Day-rates typically £900–£1,800 depending on specialism (pensions, insurance, Solvency II). Project work (full valuations, reserving studies) ranges £8,000–£40,000. Retainers (£2,000–£5,000/month) for ongoing advisory roles. Pricing drivers: actuarial qualification level (Fellowship vs Associate), specialism (insurance vs pensions), complexity of risk exposure, regulatory requirement urgency.

sales_motion: Triggered by regulatory event (Solvency II return deadline, pension scheme valuation triennial), acquisition or merger, or change in risk profile. Sold through pension consultants, insurance brokers, corporate finance advisors, and direct relationships with CFOs and scheme trustees. Conversion mechanism: demonstrated regulatory expertise and prior work on similar risk profiles.
proof_notes: Buyer requires FIA or IFoA qualification (Fellowship essential for senior roles). Evidence of successful valuations, Solvency II returns, or regulatory submissions mandatory. References from other boards, trustees, and regulators persuasive. Professional indemnity insurance and regulatory registration critical.
failure_modes: Regulatory interpretation changes: FCA, PRA, and TPR guidance shifts; model assumptions become invalid and expertise gaps emerge.
Assumption credibility risk: if market conditions (interest rates, mortality) shift sharply, actuarial assumptions come under scrutiny and advisor credibility damaged.
Fee resistance: businesses often perceive actuarial work as commodity; pressure to discount below commercial rates.
Liability exposure: material modelling error (e.g. understated reserve, miscalculated capital requirement) creates direct liability.
Succession/knowledge concentration: actuarial work requires deep technical depth; knowledge gaps emerge if lead advisor unavailable.
expansion_path: Expansion into risk management advisory (risk committee support, risk culture), insurance broking support (placement advisory), or enterprise risk advisory. Some advisors build capability in climate risk quantification and ESG risk metrics.

Commoditisation and digital disruption: robo-advisors and DIY platforms erode fee justification for simple portfolios.
expansion_path: Expansion into family office advisory (governance, reporting, manager selection), corporate trustee work, or estate planning (coordination with legal counsel). Some advisors shift into impact/ESG investment advisory.

target_buyer: Head of Compliance, Chief Risk Officer, MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer), or Chief Compliance Officer.

Pricing drivers: firm size, customer base complexity, regulatory scrutiny level, geographic footprint (multi-jurisdictional).

sales_motion: Triggered by regulatory event: FCA/PRA inspection notice, sanctions list review, M&A regulatory requirement, or business expansion into higher-risk jurisdictions. Sold through compliance consultants, law firms, and direct relationships with COOs and CROs. Conversion mechanism: demonstrated regulatory credibility (prior FCA/PRA experience) and evidence of successful compliance remediation.
proof_notes: Buyer expects prior FCA/PRA or bank financial crime experience mandatory. Evidence of successful AML framework implementations or regulatory remediation persuasive. References from other compliance officers and regulatory contacts essential. Professional indemnity insurance mandatory.
failure_modes: Regulatory guidance volatility: FCA and international AML standards evolve; frameworks become misaligned with new guidance.

Customer lifecycle timing: AML frameworks are never 'finished'; ongoing maintenance and system updates erode retainer value.

False positive management: AML systems generate high false-positive rates; if advisor's framework generates excessive alerts, operational burden and cost pressure emerge.
expansion_path: Expansion into broader financial crime advisory (fraud, market abuse), sanctions advisory, or regulatory investigation support. Some advisors build capability in ESG and beneficial ownership verification.

name: DPO-as-a-Service / Privacy Advisory
description: Part-time Data Protection Officer function for organisations that need a DPO but cannot justify a full-time hire, providing ROPA (Record of Processing Activities) maintenance, DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) facilitation, breach management, and SAR (Subject Access Request) handling. The independent DPO acts as the embedded privacy officer, supporting GDPR compliance and data governance. Ideal for scale-ups, SMEs, and non-UK organisations needing UK representation.
target_customer: SMEs to mid-market businesses (50–500 staff) and non-UK companies requiring UK data protection officer. Sectors: SaaS, digital marketing, healthcare tech, fintech, e-commerce.
target_buyer: Head of Legal, Compliance Officer, IT Director, or Managing Director in smaller firms.
core_service: ROPA development, maintenance, and process documentation
GDPR compliance and data governance oversight
Data breach management and notification support
Data controller and processor relationship management

pricing_range.notes: Retainers typically £800–£2,500/month depending on organisation size, data volumes, and processing complexity. Some advisors offer tiered packages (£800/month basic, £1,500/month with breach support, £2,500/month full governance). Pricing drivers: employee count, data subject categories, processing complexity (AI, profiling), regulatory sector (finance, health).

sales_motion: Triggered by regulatory event: subject to mandatory DPO requirement (financial services, health, public sector), major GDPR audit finding, or breach incident. Sold through compliance consultants, law firms, IT consultants, and direct outreach to Legal/Compliance teams. Conversion mechanism: GDPR audit gap assessment showing compliance exposure; cost comparison to permanent hire.
proof_notes: Buyer expects IAPP (International Association of Privacy Professionals) certification (CIPL or CIPP) mandatory. Evidence of successful DPA/ICO engagement and breach handling persuasive. References from other DPOs and legal counsel in similar sectors essential. Professional indemnity insurance critical.
failure_modes: Regulatory interpretation changes: ICO and DPA guidance evolve; ROPA and process documentation become misaligned.
Breach timing and liability: if breach occurs post-engagement, DPO advisory may be scrutinised; liability exposure if DPO recommendations inadequate.
Data subject volume growth: as organisation scales, DPO resource requirements increase beyond retainer scope; boundary disputes and scope creep.
Conflicting requirements: multi-jurisdictional organisations face competing DPA requirements (GDPR, CCPA, LDPC); integrated advice complex.
Client engagement fatigue: GDPR compliance is never 'finished'; if retainer perceived as low-value maintenance, client tempted to bring in-house.
expansion_path: Expansion into broader data governance advisory (data strategy, AI governance, ethics), international privacy advisory (CCPA, LDPC), or information security advisory. Some advisors build capability in vendor management and data processor assessment.

name: EHS & Safety Advisory
description: Environmental, health and safety management system design and implementation, covering ISO 45001/14001 implementation, safety case development, CDM (Construction Design and Management) coordinator roles, and environmental compliance advisory. The independent advisor acts as the EHS specialist, providing strategic guidance, audit support, and operational implementation. Ideal for growing manufacturers, construction firms, and regulated industries requiring structured safety governance.
target_customer: Manufacturing, construction, and utilities businesses (50–500 staff) with high safety risk or regulatory scrutiny. Sectors: engineering, chemical, logistics, construction, facilities management.
target_buyer: Health & Safety Manager, Operations Director, or Plant Manager — occasionally the CEO in smaller organisations.
core_service: ISO 45001 / ISO 14001 implementation and certification support
Safety management system design and documentation
Safety case development and HSE liaison
CDM coordinator and site safety advisory (construction)

pricing_range.notes: Environment, health, and safety (EHS) advisory: £900-£1,300/day.

sales_motion: Triggered by regulatory event: HSE inspection notice, certification requirement (ISO 45001), safety incident, or business acquisition/expansion. Sold through construction consultants, engineering firms, insurance brokers, and direct relationships with Ops/Safety teams. Conversion mechanism: gap assessment showing HSE compliance exposure and incident risk quantification.
proof_notes: Buyer expects NEBOSH (National Examination Board in Occupational Safety and Health) or IOSH (Institution of Occupational Safety and Health) membership. Evidence of successful ISO certifications and HSE remediation persuasive. References from other H&S leads and auditors helpful. Insurance and liability cover standard.
failure_modes: Regulatory interpretation shifts: HSE guidance changes; EHS systems become misaligned with new enforcement standards.
Incident liability exposure: if major safety incident occurs post-engagement, EHS advisor's recommendations scrutinised; liability risk if system deemed inadequate.
Certification gatekeeping: once ISO certified, ongoing retainer value challenged; client perceives compliance as 'done'.
Site-specific complexity: if organisation operates multiple sites with different risk profiles, integrated EHS approach difficult and expensive.
Cost pressure in downturns: EHS perceived as non-revenue generating; budget cuts and retainer termination risk in recessions.
expansion_path: Expansion into broader risk and compliance advisory (enterprise risk, process safety), sustainability reporting (ESG, carbon accounting), or incident investigation and claims support. Some advisors build capability in supply chain safety and contractor management.

name: Quality & ISO Certification Advisory
description: ISO 9001/27001/14001/45001 implementation and certification support, QMS (Quality Management System) design, internal audit support, and GxP quality advisory for life sciences. The independent advisor acts as the quality/compliance specialist, providing certification guidance, documentation, and audit support. Ideal for organisations seeking formal quality certification, improving supplier credentials, or entering regulated sectors.
target_customer: SMEs to mid-market businesses (20–300 staff) seeking ISO certification for customer/compliance requirement. Sectors: manufacturing, software, life sciences, professional services, medical devices.
target_buyer: Quality Manager, Operations Director, or Compliance Officer.
core_service: ISO certification pathway advisory and gap assessment
Quality management system (QMS) design and documentation
Internal audit programme design and support
GxP quality advisory for regulated (pharma, medical device) environments
Certification body liaison and audit support

pricing_range.notes: ISO certification and management systems: £12k-£30k per engagement (6-12 weeks).

sales_motion: Triggered by customer requirement (supplier certification mandate), business expansion into regulated sector, or competitive requirement. Sold through quality consultants, industry associations, and direct outreach to Ops/Quality teams. Conversion mechanism: certification road map and timeline to first audit; cost comparison to in-house resource.
proof_notes: Buyer expects auditor experience (ISO lead auditor certification) or prior quality manager role. Evidence of successful certifications and satisfied client testimonials persuasive. References from certification bodies and customers helpful. Standard professional indemnity insurance.
failure_modes: Certification gatekeeping: once certified, retainer value diminishes; ongoing maintenance perceived as low-effort, creating pricing pressure.
Scope creep and documentation burden: comprehensive QMS development often exceeds initial project scope; cost overruns and client friction.
Auditor subjectivity: certification body (BSI, Lloyd's, Kiwa) auditors may challenge QMS design; rework required post-audit.
Customer audit fatigue: if customer audits are frequent, value of QMS diminishes and budget pressure emerges.
Commoditisation: larger consultancies and certification bodies increasingly bundle ISO advisory; fee compression on standard projects.
expansion_path: Expansion into broader quality and compliance advisory (EHS, data privacy), supply chain quality management, or regulatory submissions (FDA, EMA for life sciences). Some advisors shift into continuous improvement and lean/six sigma advisory.

name: Enterprise Risk Advisory
description: Board-level enterprise risk framework design and strategic advisory, including risk appetite setting, principal risk register design, risk committee support, and risk culture assessment. The independent advisor acts as the risk strategist, embedding risk governance into the organisation and supporting the board and C-suite. Ideal for mid-market and larger organisations building or maturing risk frameworks.
target_customer: Mid-market businesses (£30m–£500m revenue) and larger organisations requiring enterprise risk maturity. Sectors: financial services, insurance, large corporates, utilities, infrastructure.
target_buyer: Chief Risk Officer, Group Finance Director, Board Chair, or Audit Committee Chair.
core_service: Principal risk register and risk quantification
Risk committee structure and remit design

pricing_range.notes: Day-rates typically £700–£1,300/day. Retainers (£2,000–£5,000/month) for ongoing CRO advisory and risk committee support. Project work (full ERM implementation) ranges £20,000–£80,000. Pricing drivers: organisation complexity, ERM maturity level, regulatory sensitivity (insurance, banking), governance intensity.

sales_motion: Triggered by regulatory event: audit finding, governance rating downgrade, or new regulatory guidance (e.g. revised risk management frameworks). Sold through corporate advisors, audit firms, and direct CRO relationships. Conversion mechanism: risk maturity assessment showing governance gaps and board-level impact; benchmark against peers.
proof_notes: Buyer expects prior Chief Risk Officer or equivalent board-level risk role. Evidence of successful ERM implementations and risk appetite frameworks persuasive. References from other boards, audit committees, and regulators helpful. Professional indemnity insurance and D&O liability cover recommended.
failure_modes: Framework adoption resistance: if board or C-suite lacks risk appetite for detailed governance, framework becomes 'tick-box' and retainer perceived as low-value.
Regulatory interpretation volatility: risk frameworks become misaligned with new regulatory guidance (PRA, FCA, industry-specific).
Liability exposure: if major risk materialises post-engagement, ERM framework scrutinised; advisor blamed for inadequate risk identification.
Leadership turnover: if new CRO or CFO arrives with different risk philosophy, existing framework becomes obsolete and engagement at risk.
Resource concentration: if advisor is the sole relationship, knowledge concentration risk and client retention vulnerability emerge.
expansion_path: Expansion into broader operational risk advisory, regulatory advisory (regulatory strategy, compliance framework), or board advisory (governance, audit support). Some advisors shift into climate/ESG risk and scenario planning.

name: Corporate Strategy Advisory
description: Strategy development facilitation, competitive intelligence, market entry analysis, growth strategy, board strategy workshops, and scenario planning for mid-market and larger organisations. The independent advisor acts as the strategy sparring partner and facilitator, supporting the CEO and board in setting long-term direction and M&A strategy. Typically project-based or retained for ongoing strategic advisory.
target_customer: Mid-market to large businesses (£50m–£500m revenue) at growth inflection or facing strategic challenge. Sectors: software, industrials, professional services, healthcare, consumer.
target_buyer: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Strategy Officer, or Board Chair.
core_service: Growth strategy and market entry planning

pricing_range.notes: Project work (full strategy development) typically £10,000–£80,000 depending on scope and duration. Retainers (£3,000–£8,000/month) for ongoing CEO advisory and strategy governance. Some advisors offer workshop-based pricing (£5,000–£15,000 per session). Pricing drivers: project complexity, competitive landscape intensity, M&A involvement, international scope.

sales_motion: Triggered by strategic catalyst: new CEO/board appointment, growth plateau, competitive threat, or M&A opportunity. Sold through investment banks, corporate finance advisors, and direct CEO/board relationships. Conversion mechanism: strategy workshop demonstrating clear thinking on growth options and competitive positioning; board credibility.
proof_notes: Buyer expects evidence of prior strategy work (consulting firm, corporate strategy role, or successful strategy outcomes). Case studies of market entry or growth strategy persuasive. References from other CEOs and boards essential. Network within buyer's sector and investor base valuable.
failure_modes: Board alignment challenges: if board lacks consensus on strategic direction, advisor becomes politically exposed and blamed for 'weak facilitation'.
External market disruption: if strategy becomes obsolete due to market shift post-engagement, advisor credibility damaged.
Execution failure: if strategy developed but not executed, buyer frustration emerges; perceived as 'ivory tower' advice.
Advice commoditisation: larger consulting firms commoditise strategy work; fee compression on standard market entry or growth advisory.
Long sales cycles and low conversion: strategy advisory requires deep trust; significant pre-sales effort with low conversion rates.
expansion_path: Expansion into change management advisory (strategy execution), digital transformation, or operational improvement. Some advisors shift into private equity advisory or board placement.

name: Organisational Design Advisory
description: Organisation structure redesign, operating model design, spans and layers analysis, job architecture and grading, and workforce planning. The independent advisor acts as the organisational design specialist, helping businesses align structure to strategy and improve operating efficiency. Typically project-based, with implementation support often separating from design.
target_customer: Mid-market to large businesses (100–2,000+ staff) undergoing transformation, merger, or operational restructure. Sectors: financial services, technology, professional services, manufacturing, utilities.
target_buyer: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer, or Chief HR Officer.
core_service: Organisation structure design and span analysis

pricing_range.notes: Project work (full organisational redesign) typically £8,000–£50,000 depending on complexity and scope. Larger transformations (multi-site, complex grading) £30,000–£50,000. Day-rate work (£700–£1,200/day) for implementation support and change management. Pricing drivers: organisation size, complexity (functions, geographies), urgency, cultural sensitivity.

sales_motion: Triggered by corporate event: merger/integration, cost restructure, strategic pivot, or CEO/COO change. Sold through change management consultants, HR consultants, and direct COO/CEO relationships. Conversion mechanism: current-state assessment showing structural inefficiency or operating cost opportunity; benchmark against comparable organisations.
proof_notes: Buyer expects prior organisational design experience (consulting firm, corporate HR/OD role, or successful restructure outcomes). Case studies of operating model redesigns persuasive. References from other COOs/CEOs and HR leaders essential. Evidence of successful implementation (not just design) valuable.
failure_modes: Implementation failure: if designed structure is not implemented or resisted by leaders, advisor blamed for 'impractical design'.
Unintended consequences: new structure may create new problems (silos, accountability gaps, morale issues) that weren't anticipated.
Change management complexity: organisation design often triggers significant cultural/political resistance; implementation requires change management skills beyond design.
Talent and retention risk: if redesign eliminates roles or creates redundancy, key talent may depart; advisor implicated.
External market shifts: if external conditions change during design-to-implementation, redesigned structure becomes misaligned.
expansion_path: Expansion into change management advisory (implementation support), HR advisory (talent/culture), or broader transformation advisory. Some advisors build capability in remote/hybrid working models and agile organisational design.

name: Restructuring & Turnaround Advisory
description: Distressed business advisory supporting working capital stabilisation, creditor negotiation, operational cost restructuring, turnaround plan development, and lender-side advisory. The independent advisor acts as the turnaround specialist, providing strategic and operational guidance to improve cash position and viability. Ideal for businesses in financial distress, under lender scrutiny, or facing significant operational challenge.
target_customer: Mid-market businesses (£5m–£200m revenue) in financial distress, facing covenant breach, significant cash burn, or operational crisis. Also: lenders (banks, PE firms) requiring independent portfolio assessment.
target_buyer: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, or Lender (Bank, PE firm — VP of Portfolio or Credit Officer).
core_service: Distressed business assessment and viability analysis
Working capital optimisation and cash preservation
Operational cost restructuring and efficiency improvement
Turnaround plan development and lender reporting

pricing_range.notes: Day-rates typically £900–£1,800/day for operational work. Some advisors work on retainer basis (£2,000–£5,000/month) during turnaround execution. Success fees (% of cash improvement or deal value) common, ranging 5–15% of realised value. Pricing drivers: business complexity, distress severity, turnaround timeline, creditor involved.

sales_motion: Triggered by crisis event: covenant breach notice, lender demand, cash flow crisis, or major loss/customer loss. Sold through turnaround advisors, restructuring lawyers, and banks. Conversion mechanism: rapid diagnostic call showing cash impact and turnaround options; lender or board credibility.
proof_notes: Buyer expects prior turnaround experience (restructuring firm, in-house turnaround CFO, or lender portfolio role). Evidence of successful business salvage or cash improvement persuasive. References from other lenders and turnaround professionals essential. Ability to work at pace and manage creditor complexity critical.
failure_modes: Business viability misassessment: if turnaround plan is unrealistic, creditor confidence lost and restructuring fails.
Creditor conflicted interests: different creditor classes have conflicting incentives; advisor caught in cross-fire and blamed for poor outcomes.
Execution failure: if turnaround plan is well-designed but not executed, advisor credibility damaged and lender relationships suffer.
Personal liability risk: in insolvency, advisor recommendations may be scrutinised by liquidators or regulators; professional indemnity insurance critical.
Time intensity and burn-out: turnaround work is intensive; if timeline extends, advisor resource and profitability erodes.
expansion_path: Expansion into insolvency advisory or lender advisory (distressed portfolio management). Some advisors shift into M&A advisory (distressed seller support) or corporate finance (stress-tested forecasting).

The independent HR Director acts as the fractional senior leader, embedded into the organisation or serving on an advisory board. Ideal for growing SMEs that need sophisticated HR leadership but cannot justify permanent senior hire.
target_customer: Growth-stage SMEs (50–300 staff) with expanding HR complexity, high-growth tech, or scaling professional services. Sectors: software, professional services, healthcare tech, finance tech, manufacturing.
target_buyer: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer, or Managing Director.
core_service: Recruitment process design and hiring support
Organisational culture and employee engagement advisory

pricing_range.notes: Retainers typically £1,500–£4,000/month depending on organisation size, HR maturity, and complexity. Lower end for advisory/strategic guidance; higher end for operational involvement (recruitment, ER cases). Pricing drivers: employee count, HR function maturity, growth rate, industry sector (higher for regulated/unionised).

sales_motion: Triggered by HR scaling trigger: rapid headcount growth, first employment tribunal case, management complaints about HR gaps, or CEO concern about culture. Sold through recruitment consultants, business coaches, and direct CEO relationships. Conversion mechanism: HR diagnostic showing gaps in policy, risk exposure, or capability; cost comparison to permanent hire.
proof_notes: Buyer expects CIPD (Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development) qualification or equivalent, plus prior HR director/senior manager experience. Evidence of successful culture transformation or HR scaling persuasive. References from other CEOs and business advisors helpful. Employment law and compliance knowledge essential.
failure_modes: Organisational outgrowth: as organisation scales beyond 300 staff, fractional model becomes insufficient; upgrade to permanent hire required.
ER and legal complexity: if significant ER dispute or employment tribunal case arises, liability exposure emerges; advisor blamed for inadequate policy.
Cultural fit challenge: HR is often personality-driven; if advisor doesn't fit culture or leadership style, relationship fractures quickly.
Confidentiality and trust issues: if confidential HR information leaks or advisor perceived as politically biased, trust erodes.
Commoditisation and offshore HR: increasing availability of HR platforms and offshore HR support erodes retainer justification.
expansion_path: Expansion into change management advisory (culture transformation), organisational design (structure and roles), or broader people advisory (talent acquisition, leadership coaching). Some advisors shift into board advisory or interim management.

name: Employee Relations Advisory
description: Retained advisory support for complex employee relations matters. SMEs and growth companies retain an experienced ER professional to navigate disciplinary cases, disputes, redundancy programmes, and tribunal risk without paying for a full-time in-house team or expensive law firm retainers.
target_customer: Growth companies (50–300 headcount) and scale-ups managing their first significant ER challenges. Also mid-market companies replacing legal retainers with experienced ER practitioners.
target_buyer: Head of People, CHRO, or sometimes a Managing Director or Operations lead in smaller companies.
core_service: On-call ER advisory for complex cases: guidance on performance management, disciplinary/grievance processes, redundancy programmes, TUPE transfers, settlement negotiations, and Employment Tribunal risk mitigation. Typically includes case review, evidence assessment, process design, and coaching for difficult conversations.
commercial_model: Monthly retainer (typically £2,500–£6,000/month for a few hours per week on-call support, plus day rates for larger projects like redundancy programmes at £750–£1,200/day). Some practitioners offer 'retainer + project spike' pricing, where the retainer covers small advice and occasional hours, with additional fees for major initiatives.

pricing_range.notes: £2,500–£7,000/month (retainer) or £750–£1,200/day (project basis)

sales_motion: Warm introduction via employment law firms, accountants, or peers. Often triggered by a specific ER crisis (redundancy, tribunal threat, disciplinary escalation). First conversation focuses on the immediate problem; retainer proposal follows once trust is established. Often sold as '6-month trial' at the beginning to reduce buyer friction.
proof_notes: Case studies of successful tribunal defence or redundancy execution. Testimonials from employment law firms (high credibility). Specific expertise in the buyer's industry if possible (financial services, tech, manufacturing all have ER peculiarities). LinkedIn recommendations from previous HR clients.
failure_modes: Scope creep: retainer becomes bottomless because ER casework is never truly 'finished'. Need to actively manage scope and escalate unexpected work.
Under-delivery on quick response: buyers expect on-call availability. If you're slow to reply or unavailable when needed, they'll switch to a law firm.
Becoming the in-house ER person: risk of being pulled into ongoing line management or casework that should be handled in-house. Need to coach, not do.
expansion_path: Successful ER retainers often expand to other HR advisory work (strategy, compliance, policy). Some practitioners move into interim CHRO roles once they've earned trust. High-growth path: build a small team of ER practitioners and scale to multiple retained clients.

name: Reward & Compensation Design
description: Project-based design of pay structures, job levelling frameworks, bonus schemes, and equity arrangements. Growth companies need to move from ad-hoc pay decisions to coherent reward strategies, but don't need ongoing support after the initial design. Compensation audits (pay equity) also sit here.
target_customer: Growth companies (50–200 headcount) scaling headcount and needing structured pay decisions. Also mid-market companies post-acquisition or undertaking pay equity audits. Companies planning equity grants.
target_buyer: Head of People, CHRO, CFO (often jointly), or occasionally the CEO (if no people infrastructure yet).
core_service: Design of pay structures: job levelling frameworks, salary bands, market benchmarking, bonus scheme design, equity scheme design, benefits optimisation
May include pay equity audit, data analysis, and remediation planning
Deliverables typically include: documented job framework, salary band guidance, bonus model, communications guide, and implementation plan.
commercial_model: Fixed project fee or daily rate, typically 4–12 weeks in duration. Projects that involve significant data analysis (pay equity audits) often quoted at fixed fee to cover the intensive analytical work upfront.
sales_motion: Usually inbound: CFO/Head of People realises they need coherent pay structure. Sell via specific deliverable: 'Job levelling framework and salary band audit' (4-week project) or 'Pay equity audit and remediation plan' (6-week project). Often triggered by headcount growth, acquisition, or employee complaint. Move quickly from discovery to proposal; these projects tend to start immediately once green-lit.
proof_notes: Written case studies showing before/after (anonymised). Specific frameworks you've used (e.g., Mercer, Hay, CRG job evaluation). Data visualization examples of benchmarking analysis. CFO and Head of People testimonials (ideally both perspectives). Published writing on compensation or job levelling.
failure_modes: Over-scoping: diving too deep into perfect data when the client just needs 'good enough' to make decisions. Set clear scope upfront.
Designing frameworks that are too complex for the client to maintain. Keep it simple and handover-friendly.
Getting dragged into salary review cycles post-project: make clear that implementation and ongoing reviews are separate engagements.
expansion_path: Successful projects often lead to retained advisory relationships (annual benchmarking reviews, scheme tweaks, equity grant administration). Some practitioners offer 'Reward Strategy' retainers (£2–4k/month) post-design. Occasional expansion to fractional CFO or finance advisory in small companies.

name: Learning Programme Design & Facilitation
description: Design and delivery of learning and development programmes: leadership development cohorts, technical training, onboarding, capability building. Can be one-off programmes or series-based. Combines instructional design, facilitation, and sometimes train-the-trainer elements.
target_customer: Growth companies (30–150 headcount) investing in capability building, especially leadership development. Also mid-market companies undertaking sales enablement or technical upskilling. Companies with new skill gaps due to rapid hiring.
target_buyer: Head of People, CHRO, sometimes VP of Sales (for sales enablement) or Head of Operations (for technical training).
core_service: Design of learning programmes (needs analysis, curriculum development, learning objectives, assessment design)
Facilitation of cohort-based or classroom learning
May include: pre-work materials, cohort coaching, post-programme reinforcement, measurement
Programmes range from single-session workshops to 12-week cohort journeys.
commercial_model: Fixed fee per programme (common for defined cohorts like 'Leadership Programme for your 10 senior managers') or daily rate for open-ended advisory + facilitation. Some practitioners price as 'per participant' (£1,500–£3,500 per person for a multi-week programme).
sales_motion: Usually inbound: CEO or People Lead recognises capability gap ('We need to develop our top 10 managers' or 'We need to onboard our new sales team faster'). Sell via specific programme proposal: '12-week cohort-based leadership programme for 8 senior managers' with clear outcomes and timeline. First conversation establishes objectives; proposal follows within 1–2 weeks. Projects typically start within 4–8 weeks of agreement.
proof_notes: Case studies with learning outcomes and post-programme business impact (retention, promotion velocity, engagement scores). Client testimonials with specific quotes on impact. Curriculum samples (anonymised). Evidence of learning design methodology (ADDIE, etc.). Facilitator credentials (if relevant).
failure_modes: Over-designing programmes and missing the launch date. Set a 'minimum viable programme' scope and iterate post-launch.
Trying to be the sole facilitator for all cohorts, killing your leverage. Plan for co-facilitation or alumni facilitation from the start.
Not measuring what clients care about. Focus on business outcomes (retention, engagement, capability) not just participant satisfaction scores.
expansion_path: Successful programmes often lead to annual refreshes or new cohorts. Some practitioners move into ongoing 'Learning Strategy' retainers (£2–4k/month). High growth path: productise your most successful programme and scale facilitation through partners or LMS delivery.

name: Talent Acquisition Infrastructure Build
description: Building TA capability from the ground up: creating recruiting functions, designing hiring processes, selecting and implementing ATS systems, building sourcing playbooks, and training interview panels. Ideal for high-growth companies that need to professionalize recruiting but lack the infrastructure.
target_customer: High-growth companies (30–150 headcount) in rapid scaling phase, typically pre-Series B or Series B/C. Also companies exiting from over-reliance on agency recruiting. Tech, fintech, and software companies are ideal customers.
target_buyer: COO, VP People, Head of People, or in smaller companies the CEO/Founder.
core_service: End-to-end TA function build: hiring process design (from requisition through offer), ATS selection and implementation, recruiter training and KPI dashboards, sourcing playbook and channel mix strategy, interview training and assessor calibration, employer brand/EVP development. Deliverables include documented processes, ATS configuration, recruiter playbooks, training materials, and dashboards.
commercial_model: Project-based (fixed fee for defined scope like 'Build our TA function over 8 weeks') or phase-based (ATS implementation £8–15k, process design £6–10k, training £3–5k, ongoing support retainer). Most practitioners combine project work with a short retained advisory period (8–12 weeks) post-launch.
sales_motion: Inbound from fast-growing companies whose CEOs/COOs recognise they're losing quality hires due to slow/chaotic recruiting. Pain point is usually: 'We're growing 50% YoY but our hiring is broken, and we can't afford a full TA team yet'. Sell the complete build (typically 8–12 weeks) as a package. First conversation identifies specific pain; proposal outlines build phases and timeline. Quick close rates (often 2–4 weeks from first conversation to start).
proof_notes: Before/after case studies: hiring velocity (time-to-fill), quality metrics (retention at 6/12 months), cost-per-hire reduction. Examples of ATS implementations you've led. Testimonials from both the TA team and the hiring manager/CEO. Published writing on recruiting systems. References from previous clients (these deals are large enough that references matter).
failure_modes: Trying to over-implement ATS features rather than focusing on core hiring process. Keep it simple at first; more sophistication comes later.
Not building in enough training and handover. The client has to own this after you leave, or they'll regress.
Scope creep from 'build our TA function' into 'become our interim Head of TA'. Set clear boundaries around what you're building vs. what they own.
expansion_path: Post-build contracts often expand to 8–12 week retained advisory (£3–5k/month) as they hit new hiring phases. Some practitioners move into fractional Talent VP/Head of TA roles with clients. High growth: offer TA as a fully managed service (you run recruiting) for smaller companies that can't hire a TA lead.

name: DEI Programme Design & Implementation
description: Design and delivery of diversity, equity, and inclusion programmes and strategies: pay equity audits, inclusive hiring process design, leadership coaching on inclusive leadership, diversity data analysis, cultural competency training. Projects are typically 6–16 weeks and include strategy, design, implementation, and measurement.
target_customer: Larger companies (200+ headcount) needing to demonstrate DEI progress to stakeholders (board, investors, employees). Also PE-backed companies with DEI requirements in add-on acquisition models. Some mid-market companies with public commitments to DEI.
target_buyer: CHRO, Head of People, sometimes a dedicated Head of DEI. Board-level interest is common.
core_service: DEI strategy development, programme design, and implementation

Typical scope includes: pay equity audit and remediation planning, inclusive hiring process design with interview training, leadership coaching on bias and inclusion, diversity data analysis and reporting, cultural change roadmap
Delivers both strategic roadmap and tactical implementation in priority areas.
commercial_model: Project-based pricing (fixed fee for defined scope like 'Pay equity audit + action plan' or 'Inclusive hiring process redesign'). Some practitioners offer 'DEI Strategy Retainer' (£2–4k/month) post-project for ongoing coaching and measurement.
sales_motion: Inbound from HR leaders or board pressure (investor requirement, employee petition, public commitment). Often begins with a specific, credible entry point like 'Pay equity audit' rather than broad 'DEI strategy'. Sell data-driven, actionable projects rather than aspirational culture change. Long sales cycles (8–12 weeks) are common; buyer consensus takes time. Proposal emphasises measurement and realistic timelines rather than transformation promises.
proof_notes: Pay equity audit case studies (anonymised data showing disparity diagnosis and remediation steps). Inclusive hiring process examples with post-hire diversity metrics. Leadership coaching impact data. Thought leadership on DEI measurement and strategy. Testimonials emphasising credibility and realism (not overpromising culture change).
failure_modes: Overselling transformation potential. Real culture change takes 2–3 years; DEI programmes typically show early wins in hiring and data transparency.
Positioning DEI as ethical imperative rather than business benefit. Current political climate requires grounding in concrete business case (talent, risk, compliance).

Not staying realistic about budget constraints. Post-ESG backlash, many organisations are cutting DEI budgets or being more cautious. Price accordingly and be clear about what's achievable in the budget.
expansion_path: Successful audit/strategy projects sometimes lead to implementation support retainers (£2–4k/month for 6–12 months). Some practitioners move into ongoing 'DEI Measurement' retainers as clients execute their roadmaps. Occasional expansion to fractional Chief Diversity Officer roles in larger companies.

name: People Due Diligence
description: HR and people assessment as part of M&A, acquisition, or significant investment processes. Assess target company's people infrastructure, culture, risks (ER, turnover, key person dependencies), and integration planning. Typically done by PE, corporate development teams, or internal stakeholders managing transactions.
target_customer: Private equity firms, corporate development teams, growth equity investors, strategic acquirers. Deal sizes typically £5m–£100m+. Also management teams managing their own acquisitions.
target_buyer: Investment director, corporate development lead, managing partner, or due diligence coordinator at the acquiring organisation.
core_service: Rapid assessment (2–4 weeks typically) of target company's people function: organisational structure, talent quality, retention risks, cultural fit with acquirer, key person dependencies, ER and compliance risks, integration planning. Deliverable is usually a 'People Due Diligence Report' identifying key risks, opportunities, and integration considerations.
commercial_model: Fixed fee or daily rate, typically 5–15 days of work per engagement. Scope and timeline are usually tight (investor/PE timelines are tight). Some practitioners offer 'post-deal integration support' as an add-on.
sales_motion: Usually inbound from PE firms, corporate development teams, or investors you know. Relationship-based: PE firms and corporate development teams tend to use the same advisors repeatedly. Build relationships with 2–3 PE firms or corporate advisors who can feed you deals. First conversation is usually fast (48 hours); projects start immediately. Often triggered by specific deal that's in process.
proof_notes: References from PE firms and investors (anonymised deal experience). Example due diligence reports (heavily anonymised). Credentials in M&A or people strategy. Understanding of both corporate and PE contexts. Track record of rapid assessment and clear risk identification.
failure_modes: Over-scoping and missing tight timelines. PE timelines are immovable; you have to assess quickly and clearly.
Not understanding PE priorities. PE teams care about: retention of key people post-close, integration risks, cost reduction opportunities, and hidden liabilities. Don't spend time on nice-to-haves.
Being too diplomatic. PE and investors need clear risk identification, not softly-softly feedback. Call out red flags.
expansion_path: Successful due diligence often leads to post-deal integration support contracts (£3–8k/month for 3–6 months). Some practitioners move into fractional CHRO roles for the acquirer post-close. High growth path: become trusted advisor to a specific PE firm and take multiple deals per year.

target_customer: Fintechs, payment firms, investment managers, and other businesses seeking FCA authorisation or managing variation of permissions.

core_service: FCA authorisation and governance requirements assessment
Application pack preparation and regulatory correspondence support
Compliance and controls framework design for authorisation readiness
Governance, risk, and internal audit capability assessment
Variation of Permissions (VoP) and change of control support

pricing_range.notes: FCA authorisation advisory: £25k-£80k (straightforward financial services authorisation) to £60k-£120k (complex regulatory perimeter, multiple permissions, or novel business model). sales_motion: Fintech and payments ecosystem networks. Venture capital and PE firms investing in regulated fintech. Law firms advising on regulatory matters. Direct outreach to businesses preparing FCA authorisation applications.
proof_notes: Deep FCA authorisation knowledge and evidence of supporting multiple successful applications. Credibility with FCA and understanding of application assessment process are essential.
failure_modes: Business model scope is unclear about regulated vs unregulated activities; FCA's regulatory perimeter interpretation is strict; consultant must nail scope definition before application to avoid rework
Applicant's financial resources or governance structures are inadequate for FCA expectations; consultant must pressure-test readiness against published expectations and guide build-out
FCA feedback or queries during assessment process reveal gaps in original application; consultant must anticipate FCA concerns and build robust evidence base, not just submit and react
Timelines slip because supporting evidence (business plans, compliance frameworks, financial projections) is incomplete or unconvincing; front-loading evidence gathering is critical
Post-approval, approved business model diverges from FCA assessment assumptions; consultant must clarify scope boundaries and post-approval reporting obligations to avoid compliance breach

FCA imposes conditions or prudential requirements that conflict with business plan; consultant must understand that outcome is not always approval-as-hoped; business case must be stress-tested against realistic FCA requirements
expansion_path: Ongoing compliance advisory; regulatory risk management; governance and board advisory

description: Developing inventory strategy — safety stock policy, reorder point optimisation, slow-moving stock management, write-off reduction. Target: manufacturers and distributors with excessive inventory or chronic stockouts.

failure_modes: Current inventory system data is unreliable; consultant must spend first 2-3 weeks validating data integrity or recommendations will lack credibility
Demand forecasting is inaccurate or sales/marketing is not providing pipeline data; optimisation model is only as good as demand inputs; forecast validation is essential

expansion_path: Demand forecasting, S&OP, inventory management system

name: Supply Chain Digitalisation Advisory
description: Independent advisory to mid-market and enterprise businesses selecting, scoping and implementing supply chain technology — demand planning tools, WMS, TMS, track-and-trace platforms and supply chain visibility solutions. Clients typically have budget approved and a technology mandate but lack internal capability to define requirements, run a credible vendor evaluation, or hold implementation partners accountable. The consultant closes that gap: structured requirements, vendor shortlist, RFP management, evaluation scoring, selection recommendation, and implementation roadmap.
target_customer: Mid-market manufacturers, retailers, distributors and 3PLs (£30m–£500m revenue) investing in supply chain technology without internal evaluation capability. Also larger businesses replacing legacy WMS or ERP supply chain modules.
target_buyer: Chief Supply Chain Officer, COO, or CIO — often introduced via an ERP implementation partner or a trusted procurement or operations contact
core_service: Current-state assessment and supply chain technology requirements definition
Vendor longlist and shortlist development (WMS, TMS, demand planning, visibility platforms)
RFP design, vendor scoring criteria and evaluation facilitation
Selection recommendation with commercial and implementation risk assessment
Implementation readiness and programme mobilisation advisory
Post-selection vendor governance and go-live risk advisory

pricing_range.notes: £15,000–£50,000 for requirements-through-selection engagements (4–12 weeks). Day rate £900–£1,400/day. Large enterprise WMS replacements or multi-site programmes can reach £75,000–£120,000. Retainer advisory during implementation: £3,000–£6,000/month.

sales_motion: ERP and supply chain implementation partners (SAP, Oracle, Blue Yonder, Manhattan) routinely sub-contract independent advisory to clients mid-project — these are the warmest referral sources. Direct outreach to CSCO/COO/CIO at mid-market manufacturers, retailers and distributors flagging technology investment on LinkedIn or in trade press. CILT and Supply Chain Forum events. Content marketing on LinkedIn around vendor selection mistakes and RFP design — high resonance with the exact buyer audience.
proof_notes: Technology selection case studies, vendor evaluation examples, implementation experience
failure_modes: Client conflates advisory with implementation delivery — expects the consultant to manage the programme, not just advise; scope and role boundaries must be set at engagement start
Long sales cycles to CSCO/CIO level — significant unpaid scoping and proposal work before engagement confirmation; pipeline must be broad to sustain income

Technology vendor relationships create perceived or real bias — clients may question independence if the consultant has prior vendor ties; full disclosure and a structured scoring methodology are essential
Project stalls mid-way when digital transformation budget is cut or reprioritised — no kill fee provision means sunk cost with no revenue
Client's internal IT or procurement function resists external advisory on their domain — stakeholder buy-in across functions must be secured before engagement starts, not assumed
Scope creep as the client broadens the brief from one technology category to the full supply chain technology estate — fixed-fee projects without clear scope definition become loss-making
expansion_path: Implementation governance retainer, post-go-live optimisation, second technology category (e.g., demand planning after WMS), broader supply chain transformation advisory, procurement of implementation partner services
